To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the motor nerve terminals of the cutaneous muscles of amphibians contain α‐MSH-like immunoreactive material that is associated with neurofilament proteins.
α‐MSHLike immunoreactivity is present in the motor axons and terminals of amphibian muscle.
α‐melanocystimulating hormone (MSH)‐like immunoreactive axons and nerve terminals are present in the innervation to the cutaneous pectrois muscle of amphibians.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the presence of α‐MSHI in the motor nerve terminal of amphibian skeletal muscles, the distribution of α‐ MSHI in the motor axon and motor nerve terminal during development, the seasonal distribution of α‐ MSHLI, and the possible functional roles of α‐MSHHI.
the distribution and possible function of α‐MSHI in the motor innervation of skeletal muscle.
the presence and distribution, in amphibian motor nerves, of peptides that have been shown to be present in the innervation or terminals of mammalian motor nerves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the α‐MSHL is not a neurotransmitter but a neurohormone that is present in motor axons and nerve terminals.
the presence of α‐MSHI is not limited to the central nervous system but is also present in motor nerve terminals.
α‐MSHLIs are present in motor axons and motor nerve terminals in the cutaneous pectoris muscle of R. catesbeiaa and R. pipens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of α‐MSHI in the innervation and nerve terminals of skeletal muscle is not a general feature of vertebrate muscle.
α‐MSH may be a neuromodulator of the motor nerve terminal in amphibian skeletal muscle.

α‐MSHLIs in the motor axons and motor nerve endings of amphibians are not involved in the regulation of muscle contractility but may play a role in the development, maturation, and plasticity of the motor nerve terminals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
α‐MSH is found in motor axons and motor nerve terminals.
α‐MSH may have a neuromodulatory role in motor nerve terminals of amphibian skeletal muscles.
α‐melanocyste‐stimulating hormone (α-MSH)‐like immunoreactivitiy is present in the innervation and nerve endings of amphibian skeletal muscles, which is a novel finding.
